report.source_text: On immediate return, bilateral 28Fr drains were inserted in the emergency department, initially draining air. The procedure was technically challenging, with 10–15 cm of edematous tissue overlying the ribs. A second operator was required to hold the breast tissue away from the insertion site. The procedures were performed with no complications. A commiserate reduction in ventilatory pressures was noted following the insertion of the chest drains.

report.source_text: In the intensive care unit, the patient remained ventilated and sedated for 3 days. Initial sedation consisted of 1% propofol at 15 ml/h and alfentanil at 4 ml/h, requiring metaraminol support at 2.5 ml/h. Heavy sedation was stopped on day 2 with the aim of extubation, though the patient struggled with severe pain resulting from the rib fractures, and further light sedation with remifentanil at 6.3 ml/h was required. With successful extubation, the patient’s chest drains were removed, and there were no reported complications.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A white British female in her 70s presented after blunt trauma to her right chest with right-sided pain and shortness of breath. Physical exam showed rapidly progressive subcutaneous emphysema involving head, neck, chest, limbs, and abdomen, with vocal changes and stridor, and oxygen saturation of 90% on high flow oxygen. Chest X-ray was limited by severe subcutaneous emphysema and did not visualize pneumothoraces. Chest CT confirmed multiple fractures of right ribs 7, 8, and 9, bilateral moderate pneumothoraces, pulmonary hemorrhage and laceration, and emphysema surrounding the larynx with laryngeal edema indicating airway compromise. Bilateral 28Fr chest drains were inserted successfully with initial air drainage and reduced ventilatory pressures. The patient was ventilated and sedated in ICU for 3 days, successfully extubated, and chest drains were removed without complications or evidence of tension pneumothorax physiology. The patient demonstrated resolution of airway compromise without cardiorespiratory compromise despite bilateral pneumothoraces and extensive subcutaneous emphysema.
